doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Trombone sounds Willcox admired: Arthur Pryor and the Isham Jones trombonist
summary: Willcox names Arthur Pryor as a beautiful-toned early influence and an Isham Jones trombonist whose name he cannot recall; Gallodoro mentions Pryor's actor son.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who were the trombone players whose sound that you might have liked back then?
Trombone players, who had a sound that you liked?
Well when I was a young boy, maybe twelve or thirteen, I was starting to play trombone, I don’t think anyone else ever got this but there was a trombone player by the name of Arthur Pryor.
Oh my goodness. I never met him. His son became an actor. Roger Pryor. I played his act.

Anyway, isn’t that funny that I would listen to these records you know and no jazz, you know, but he had a beautiful tone. And isn’t that funny that I have to say that Arthur Pryor impressed me. And of course well then, let’s see the trombone player with Isham Jones, I liked him too.
Go ahead, I’ll get to mine.
What was that guy, what was his name? Mark? The trombone player.
No. I can’t think. But anyway, he impressed me. I had got wind of —
